faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: If you still cannot find the answer to your question, {emailLink} or contact our team.
faq.q1: Can I install the app on my iPhone?
faq.a1: The httpSMS application works only on Android phones at the moment since Apple doesn't allow you to install a custom SMS messaging app.
faq.q2: What's the minimum supported Android version?
faq.a2: The httpSMS Android app works from Android 9 (Pie) and above. So you can install the application on your old Android phone which you don't use anymore.
faq.q3: Can I send unlimited number of messages per month?
faq.a3: We do have packages that allow up to 200,000 SMS messages per month but you can send us an email if you will like to send more messages so we create a custom plan just for you.
faq.q4: Can I change the sender of the SMS message?
faq.a4: No you cannot. When you send an SMS message using the httpSMS app it uses your SIM card to send the message so the recipient will see your phone number as the sender of the SMS. You cannot use your brand name as the sender ID.

grantPermissions.seoTitle: How to grant SEND_SMS and RECEIVE_SMS permissions on Android 14+ and 15+ - httpSMS
grantPermissions.seoDescription: In Android 15 (Vanilla Ice Cream), the SEND_SMS and RECEIVE_SMS permissions are now hard restricted. Learn how to grant these permissions step by step.
grantPermissions.intro: In Android 15 (Vanilla Ice Cream), the android.permission.SEND_SMS and android.permission.RECEIVE_SMS permissions are now hard restricted and cannot be granted via the runtime permissions interface.
grantPermissions.alert: Granting the SEND_SMS and RECEIVE_SMS permissions will allow an Android app to be able to read and send SMS messages on your phone. Make sure you trust the application before allowing these permissions.
grantPermissions.step1Desc: Long press the icon of the android app which you want to grant the permission and select App info.
grantPermissions.step2Desc: On the App Info page, click on the menu button in the top-right corner and select the Allow restricted settings option.
grantPermissions.step3Desc: Once you have allowed the restricted settings from step 2 above, navigate to Permissions ➡️ SMS and tap Allow to grant SMS permissions to the android app.
grantPermissions.conclusionDesc: Congratulations, you have successfully configured SMS permissions on your Android app.

e2eEncryption.title: Secure your conversations with end-to-end encryption for SMS messages
e2eEncryption.description: Take control of your privacy by encrypting your SMS messages end-to-end. Safeguard your messages from prying eyes, ensuring absolute confidentiality.
e2eEncryption.seoTitle: Secure your conversations with end-to-end encryption for SMS messages - httpSMS
e2eEncryption.seoDescription: Enable end-to-end encryption for your SMS messages with httpSMS so no one but you can read the texts you send and receive through your Android phone.
e2eEncryption.intro1: We have added support for end-to-end encryption for SMS messages so that no one can see the content of the messages you send using httpSMS except you.
e2eEncryption.intro2: You setup an encryption key which you use to encrypt your messages before making an API request to httpSMS and you also use the same key to decrypt the messages you receive from httpSMS via our
e2eEncryption.algorithmNote: We are using the AES-256 encryption algorithm to encrypt and decrypt the messages.
e2eEncryption.step1Desc: the httpSMS Android app on your phone and set your encryption key under the App Settings page of the app.
e2eEncryption.step2Desc1: We use the AES-256 encryption algorithm to encrypt the SMS messages. This algorithm requires an encryption key which is 256 bits; to work around this, we will hash any encryption key you set on the mobile app using the SHA-256 algorithm so that it will always produce a key which is 256 bits.
e2eEncryption.step2Desc2: The AES algorithm also has an initialization vector (IV) parameter which is used to ensure that the same value encrypted multiple times will not produce the same encrypted value. The IV is 16 bits and it is appended to the encrypted message before encoding it in Base64.
e2eEncryption.step2Desc3: When you use our client libraries it will automatically take care of encrypting your message so you don't have to deal with creating the initialization vector and encoding the payload yourself.
e2eEncryption.step3Desc: After generating the encrypted message payload, you can send it directly using the httpSMS API. Make sure to set encrypted: true in the JSON request payload so that httpSMS knows that the message is encrypted and it will be decoded in the Android app before sending to your recipient.

e2eEncryption.conclusionDesc: Congratulations, you have successfully configured your Android phone to send and receive SMS messages with end-to-end encryption.
